Hi Laura / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme Health is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for a regulated inference workload (PHI-only inference inside our VPC). Before we lock in a procurement timeline the infra team asked for concrete guidance on two things:

1) Sizing guidance for a private GPU pool that can sustain ~400 concurrent inference sessions (average request = 300 tokens, peak arrival = 18 req/s sustained for 10m windows) while meeting p95 latency < 250ms for 8k-context models.
2) Expected headroom and burst strategy if we need an additional 2x sustained capacity for seasonal surges.

Attached is our compliance summary and a short list of network constraints (acme_requirements.pdf). Can you give a short run-rate estimate and recommended warmup/warmpool strategy so our architects can sign off? Also, we will need basic SOC2 evidence pointers and a network diagram for procurement.

Thanks,

Hi Jenny — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. I pulled Marcus and Dev into this thread for infra sizing and a short runbook. High-level answers up front and then a short list of discovery questions so we can turn this into a mutual action plan (MAP).

Quick estimate (very rough, subject to discovery):
- Baseline: to sustain 18 req/s with avg 300 tokens and p95 <250ms on a 8k-context open model, expect ~6-8 A100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state (continuous batching + KV prefix caching assumed).
- Burst: for 2x sustained surge, we recommend a warm pool equivalent to 50% of surge capacity (so add 6 GPUs warm for ~30s fast absorption) + autoscale headroom to spin up remaining capacity within 5–10 minutes depending on private infra orchestration.

Initial assumptions I used for the estimate:
- Batch-friendly traffic (requests can be batched up to 32 tokens average per micro-batch)
- Quantized model variant supported (int8 or fp16) to reduce per-token service time
- Prefix/KV cache hit rate targeting 60% for conversational warm starts

Discovery ask (quick):
1) Typical request token distribution (min/avg/max) and how often clients stream partial responses.
2) Target SLA windows (p95/p99) you need for business ops vs clinical ops.
3) Network egress constraints and whether you can provision an internal NAT/gateway for controlled egress.

I'll attach a short XLS with the rough runway estimate and a simple cost/throughput tradeoff table. Can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow at 11am PT to walk through the assumptions?

Best,

Adding technical detail to Laura's estimates (putting numbers inline so Acme infra can eyeball quickly). Assumptions / conservative sizing below — happy to refine after data.

Assumptions: 8k-context model (decoder-only), quantized to fp16 or int8, batching window 15ms target, KV cache hit 60%. Target p95 <250ms end-to-end (model forward + micro-batching latency + network).

Per-GPU steady throughput (conservative):
- Avg request = 300 tokens -> avg generation compute per request ~ 0.18 GPU-seconds (with quantized kernels, warm KV).
- So 1 GPU can serve ~5.5 requests/sec steady when fully batched and if effective batching achieved.

Sizing math (steady):
- Required sustainable req/s = 18 req/s -> 18 / 5.5 = 3.3 -> round up to 4 GPUs for compute alone.
- Add 50% for headroom + networking variance -> 6 GPUs.

Burst model (2x sustained = 36 req/s):
- Immediate absorb: warm pool strategy to quickly serve first 30–60s of surge. Warm pool size recommendation = 50% of burst capacity = 6 GPUs (warm).
- Autoscale delta: remaining capacity = 36req/s capacity -> ~7 GPUs total needed; autoscales to 7–10 GPUs based on queueing policies.

Operational notes and network impact:
- KV/prefix cache effectiveness dramatically reduces compute per request; recommend instrumenting traced token-level cache hit-rate in early pilot.
- Warm pool adds memory/kv residency cost; ensure your VPC peering/NAT rules allow internal pull of model artifacts during warmup without blocking (pre-stage artifacts to local disk where possible).
- Egress: if telemetry/logs are sent to a central Redwood console, give us an egress IP range or we can run without egress (audit-friendly) but that will affect observability features.

I'll attach a CSV with the per-GPU throughput assumptions and a small sensitivity table (varying kv hit 30/60/80%).

- Marcus
